newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds dragged down amid U.S. rate worries.
newsitem.headline: Bunds dragged down amid U.S. rate worries.

text.p: German Bunds and futures ended a dull session in softer ground on Tuesday awaiting the outcome of the U.S. Federal Reserve policy-setting meeting.
Traders said that although the prospect of possible tightening in U.S. interest rates was dominating the market, an undercurrent of domestic budget problems was also adding to Bunds' woes.

By 1446 GMT, the DTB June Bund future was trading 26 basis points lower at 101.58, while September futures were 29 basis points lower at 100.54. The June contract traded in a range from 101.36 up to 101.70 during the session.

"The burdens from the U.S. and from German government finances are likely to argue in favour of a mild consolidation in the near term," analysts at Trinkhaus Capital Management said in a research note.

But they added that with a supportive German eocnomic fundamental background, any major setbacks in Bund prices should be seen as buying opportunities, particularly in the six- and seven-year area of the cash market.
The 10-year cash benchmark Bund was holding up relatively well in the face of futures' weakness, trading six basis points lower on the day at 101.40 for a bid yield of 5.807 percent.

Only around half of U.S. economists polled by Reuters expect the Tuesday's FOMC meeting to lead to a tightening of monetary policy, and analysts said this meant debt markets were at risk if a rate hike were to materialise.

"The German market is still in a net long position. It is still a little bit overbought and if we were to get a rate rise decision tonight, we could see a good sell-off here," said Dirk Aufderheide at DMG futures and options in Frankfurt.
He said that after recent softer economic data from the U.S., he did not expect a tightening and that it would take the market by surpise if the Fed were to move.
Options markets, too, showed volatility levels ticking up in Bund trade ahead of the FOMC meeting.
On spreads, the German market outclassed U.S. Treasuries, bloating the 10-year spread to 105 basis points by 1514 GMT from around 101 basis points at the open.
